record.title: BigHat reports AI-assisted optimization of two antibody families in an automated lab
record.summary: BigHat’s October 27 report describes a collaboration in which an Anthropic researcher and Claude worked with BigHat scientists and an automated laboratory to optimize two therapeutic-antibody families. BigHat says it synthesized and tested 1,232 antibodies across seven iterative rounds in ten weeks; Anthropic’s account of the same collaboration gives a total of about 1,010 variants. Neither account explains the difference. BigHat reports selected binding, solution-stability and aggregation improvements. These are company-reported results without independent reproduction; they do not establish therapeutic efficacy or an isolated model contribution.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: BigHat published an October 27, 2026 report describing a collaboration with Anthropic on AI-assisted therapeutic-antibody optimization.

claims.label: DISPUTED
claims.text: The two partner accounts report different totals for the same ten-week BigHat/Anthropic antibody-optimization collaboration: BigHat reports 1,232 antibodies synthesized and tested, while Anthropic says about 1,010 variants. The reports do not explain whether their counting units or inclusion criteria differ.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: BigHat reports selected variants with up to ninefold tighter target binding, up to 18°C higher solution stability than starting antibodies, and slower aggregation; some samples did not fully aggregate at the instrument limit of 85°C.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The company reports that BigHat’s Reccy lab-control and data system exposed sample, instrument, protocol, raw-output and quality-control data to Claude through MCP; the collaboration also changed a thermal-stability assay after the team judged default instrument software outputs misleading.

contradictory_evidence: Anthropic’s October 27 account says BigHat made and tested about 1,010 variants in about ten weeks (lines 40–43); BigHat’s October 27 report says 1,232 antibodies were synthesized and comprehensively tested in ten weeks across seven rounds. Neither reviewed account reconciles the totals or defines a shared counting denominator. Preserve both as partner-reported figures; do not select or average them.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported experiments and outcomes are first-party company claims; no independent reproduction or underlying data audit was performed.
Only two antibody families were studied, and the reported 3–5x cycle-time comparison is not backed here by a matched comparator dataset or protocol.
Human scientists, Claude, BigHat’s laboratory, Reccy and iterative assay changes contributed together; the report does not isolate model causal contribution or establish therapeutic efficacy.
BigHat reports 1,232 antibodies, while Anthropic reports about 1,010 variants for the same ten-week collaboration; the unit, inclusion rule and relation between these counts are not explained.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, iterative AI-assisted wet-lab optimization could affect antibody lead-development throughput and the role of standardized data and lab-control systems. The current source reports one company collaboration over two antibody families and does not establish general or therapeutic outcomes.
limitations: The evidence is a BigHat-authored report about its collaboration with Anthropic; the reported numerical outcomes have not been independently reproduced in this review.
Results cover two antibody families and selected optimized variants; they do not establish broader transfer to other targets, molecules or laboratories.
BigHat’s statement that comparable lab cycles take 3–5 times longer is not a matched quantitative comparison in the reviewed source.
One Anthropic researcher, Claude, BigHat scientists, automated laboratory equipment, Reccy and iterative assay refinement were combined; no causal ablation isolates the model contribution.
Affinity, stability and aggregation measurements are preclinical engineering properties and do not establish drug safety, efficacy or clinical benefit.
BigHat and Anthropic report different totals for variants made/tested (1,232 versus about 1,010); their counting basis is unresolved.
brief.summary: BigHat’s October 27 report describes a collaboration in which an Anthropic researcher and Claude worked with BigHat scientists and an automated laboratory to optimize two therapeutic-antibody families. BigHat says it synthesized and tested 1,232 antibodies across seven iterative rounds in ten weeks; Anthropic’s account of the same collaboration gives a total of about 1,010 variants. Neither account explains the difference. BigHat reports selected binding, solution-stability and aggregation improvements. These are company-reported results without independent reproduction; they do not establish therapeutic efficacy or an isolated model contribution.

technical.claimed_result: BigHat reports selected variants with up to ninefold tighter binding, up to 18°C higher solution stability and slower aggregation. BigHat reports 1,232 antibodies synthesized/tested, while Anthropic reports about 1,010 variants for the same collaboration; this count discrepancy is unresolved.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model inference cost, full labor cost or total economic return is reported in the reviewed source. BigHat says similar cycles typically take 3–5 times longer, but a matched comparator was not provided in the reviewed material.
technical.demonstrated_result: The BigHat report and its description of a collaborative lab workflow are directly accessible. The numerical experimental outcomes are company-reported and were not independently reproduced.
technical.implementation_status: A reported collaborative preclinical research pilot involving two antibody families; therapeutic safety, efficacy and clinical use are not established.
technical.mechanism: Claude interacted through MCP with BigHat’s Reccy data/control system and automated laboratory workflow. BigHat scientists synthesized and measured designs, reviewed raw instrument outputs and quality flags, and collaborated on assay changes across iterative design-build-test rounds.
technical.novelty: A partner-reported iterative AI-assisted antibody optimization study combining sequence design, an automated wet lab, traceable experimental data and scientist-led assay refinement.
technical.regime: Two antibody families (one VHH and one scFv), seven iterative design rounds and ten weeks, according to the partner reports. BigHat reports 1,232 antibodies synthesized/tested; Anthropic says about 1,010 variants. Selected binding, thermal-stability and aggregation outcomes are reported, but the count definitions differ or are unclear.
technical.reproducibility: Both partner accounts are public; no underlying shared dataset, independent reproduction or independent audit was inspected. The reported variant totals are inconsistent and unexplained.
technical.strongest_baseline: The starting antibodies and their baseline measurements. The reported 3–5x comparison with typical laboratory cycles lacks a matched comparator in the reviewed source.

brief.title: BigHat reports AI-assisted optimization of two antibody families in an automated lab
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced, iterative model-assisted design-build-test loops could affect how quickly antibody candidates are optimized and highlight the importance of standardized, traceable lab data. This report covers two company-led preclinical projects; it does not establish transfer to other programs, overall cost savings, clinical efficacy or a Claude-only contribution.
